title: Should i go for a android or steam launch?
author: quilzao
selftext:
Hi guys, first time developing a game with 100% help of AI. Im not a dev and i dont know how to code, however im having a lot of fun during the process.

 i think my game looks like more a mobile game, but im in serious doubt if i try to launch it first on steam. What do you think?

Link: [https://estel.games/](https://estel.games/)

comments.author: BenTheSodaman
comments.body:
OP, Steam will charge you 100 USD to put your game on Steam after you go through the process. It can be a learning process. 

As a disclaimer, I'm not the target audience of the game you're sharing with us, so I can't exactly advise on what you could do next. 

e.g., flashing the keyboard controls on the screen somewhere and making sure they aren't so hardcoded that an AZERTY keyboard has a heads-up that ZQSD isn't going to work for them and might use the arrow keys. Or that spacebar is the jump key. 

Taking advantage of having slightly larger font with all the screen space available to you. 

A pause feature / button (e.g., say if someone is eight minutes in and pizza delivery rings the doorbell, but they don't want to throw their 8-minute run for a slice o' pizza.)

Consider adding a small shadow beneath the player when they're jumping. 

Some carrot on the stick unlockable / meta-progression system to give players an incentive to try again with unlocked abilities / combinations and/or difficulty modifiers (seeing the new ghosts show up sooner, but map changes sooner), etc.

Eventual running animation on the bear. Maybe a nervous sweat on the bear as ghosts get too close. And/or a game over animation / e.g., bear cowering in fear as the ghosts catch up to it. 

But as I said, I'm not the target audience of the game. So some of these suggestions might be "bleh" to your target audience.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
You don't need to "launch" anything.

This is like a game a real game dev would make while they are learning. 

If you really want to make something that will be worth people's time then focus on learning some game dev, at least either asset creation or coding. 

We're quickly moving to a time where anyone can make something like this in a few minutes. At that point nobody will be interested in playing these quick little fun for 2 minutes type of games because they can just make their own.

This is unfortunately the definition of AI slop games and we need less of them being posted to platforms.
People constantly complain here about AI haters but people flooding platforms with low effort content are  one of the reasons for it.

Nobody wants to go to Steam or itch and have to scroll through pages of slop. It's already getting bad on itch where every other asset or game now is AI generated.

Just have fun creating stuff until you can make something good. 

Nobody publishes their first drawing in an art gallery.
